Node type encodings, slot and pivot capacities, gap table presence per type and metadata bit layout.
Allocation source for fresh nodes, failure handling, reclamation timing and grace period requirements.

findings.text: Transient spanning buffer tracks a contiguous key interval with lower and upper bounds plus staged pivots and slots, a leaf level height, a total entry tally, a split position, counts of active sources and destinations, and ordered tables of source views and fresh destination nodes with per destination gap summaries.

Each source view records a node address with its type tag, an inclusive retained span expressed as start and finish indexes, and a ceiling key used when the span ends beyond stored pivots. Each destination records a fresh node address with its type tag and the ceiling key eventually achieved by streaming.

Write cursors pair a traversal view holding sought interval and current position and bounds and depth with a cached write view holding node address and type tag and pivot and slot tables, safe covering bounds for the current position, end markers for overwritten extent, and staged prior content with replacement entry.

Leaf staging creates entries for a left split when left safe start precedes sought start, always creates a central entry ending at sought finish, and creates a right split when right retained end extends beyond sought finish. Lower bound comes from left safe start, upper bound from final staged pivot, and height denotes leaf level.

Total tally adds retained entries before left position plus staged central entries plus retained entries from right resume point onward. When the affected span touches an interior boundary and the tally is at most the minimum occupancy for the side type, one adjacent sibling view is located and its occupancy is added, otherwise the sibling marker is cleared.

Destination sizing keeps one node when the total fits in the target type capacity, otherwise aims at two balanced halves. When the total exactly fills twice capacity on leaves, the split is shifted to avoid finishing a destination on an empty slot by scanning source occupancy. If neither one nor two nodes suffice, the total is divided into three parts and each destination receives a fresh node of the target type.

Source assembly follows left sibling then left retained prefix with ceiling trimmed to staged lower bound minus one, then the central staged buffer, then right retained suffix from resume point onward, then right sibling. A sibling is included only when marked nonempty and lying strictly outside the corresponding side bound.

Bulk transfer streams variable length chunks from sources in order into destinations in order, tracking per destination fill and global progress. Ceiling propagation uses the last moved source pivot when inside pivot capacity else the source ceiling, updates the destination ceiling accordingly, and bulk moves remaining pivots and slots and gaps.

When a non maximal destination would end on an empty slot, one entry is returned to the source stream by rewinding either into the prior source tail or within the current source, the split is extended by one, progress counters are decremented, and the destination ceiling is taken from the preceding pivot. The last destination consumes the remaining tally.

Finalisation clears unused trailing slots and gaps and pivots beyond the last valid index, selects the largest gap position for interior nodes that carry gaps, and records end metadata, always for the augmented range type and for other types only when the node is not completely full. Leaf metadata helper skips recording when the node is full.

Bulk move copies slots then conditionally copies gaps when the destination supports them, repairs parent links of moved children when a non leaf destination receives staged children, and propagates ceilings as described above while leaving metadata to a later finalisation step.

Data end resolution for augmented range nodes uses stored metadata, reports empty for dead nodes, uses metadata when the trailing pivot is empty, reports the last pivot position when trailing pivot equals view maximum, and otherwise reports full pivot capacity.

Safe lower bound is the preceding pivot plus one for nonzero positions and the view minimum for position zero. Setup caches node address with type tag and pivot and slot tables and derives safe covering bounds for the current position from view bounds and pivot contents.

Write walk locates the first pivot covering the sought index within the valid entry count, clamps the covering interval to view bounds, and records position and end markers. Dense nodes instead collapse the covering interval to the single sought index and reset position and index to view minimum.

Sibling search ascends both side cursors together, preferring a right advance when room remains on the right and otherwise a left retreat when room remains on the left, then descends along extreme edges to leaf level and returns the reached view. The loop repeats toward the root and signals a fault if no sibling exists.

Spanning ascent first folds a nonempty sibling into whichever side bound it extends, converts fresh destinations into staged slots with ceilings and gap summaries, handles possible new root creation, stops with parent repair when converged to one destination on a shared node, and otherwise increments height and ascends both write cursors for another round.

New root handling applies only to the full key span. Multiple destinations are packed into a single fresh range node whose flavour depends on allocation accounting mode, staged as one slot with incremented height. Whether single or multiple, the parent link is repaired and the traversal view is reset to full span with zero depth and locked root.

Write walk iterates descend with prior content sampling until a leaf type is reached, traversing down through interior levels by narrowing view bounds to the covering interval and deepening depth. Null extension then widens empty sided bounds toward safe edges and steps into adjacent empty slots to enable coalescing.

Single node store rebuilds pivots and slots by copying the retained prefix, optionally inserting a left split entry, storing the central replacement entry with its finish, then copying the retained suffix with ceiling fixups and metadata. Narrow slot store instead overwrites one or two adjacent positions in place and refreshes gap accounting when empties are involved.

Node replacement declares that the tree write lock is held by the caller and receives current tree height from a dedicated query helper. Stores choose fresh node allocation with old node reclamation when read copy update mode is active and reuse buffer overwrite in place otherwise, with gap refresh around publication.

Freshly built copy nodes and staged slots must remain invisible to readers until publication through the ordered assignment path, because the lightweight initialisation used during staging can be reordered by the compiler and would expose torn state if published early.

Fault helpers flag unreachable logic states such as missing sibling at root, streamed progress falling short of total when destinations are exhausted, and narrow expansion attempted while read copy update mode is active. One path also validates that the staged new root slot matches the expected node.

The full key universe runs from zero to the maximum unsigned long value. Interior versus root decisions and interior sibling inclusion tests and maximal destination checks all treat these extremes as sentinels.

Spanning rebalance exposes destination sizing, source assembly, and streaming transfer as callable stages that prepare fresh nodes, order retained and staged sources around the central buffer, and stream them into balanced destinations with null and ceiling handling.

Cursor maintenance exposes setup and ascend helpers that refresh cached node views from traversal position and move write cursors one level upward while recomputing valid entry counts and resume markers for the next spanning round.
Typeless allocations obtained for fresh destinations and the transient buffer viewed as a node are converted to node pointers through a dedicated cast helper.
